source.title: Local and Global Methods in Data Mining: Basic Techniques and Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Let R be a set of Boolean attributes, let the data consist of 0-1 rows over R, and let P be a class of patterns represented by Boolean expressions over those attributes. For a fixed support threshold, determine structural conditions on the pattern class P under which there is an efficient algorithm that finds exactly those patterns in P that are satisfied by at least the given fraction of rows of the data set.

evidence.quote: Problem 1 Consider 0-1 data and a class P of patterns defined as boolean expressions. Under what conditions for P is there an efficient algorithm for finding those patterns θ ∈ P that are true for at least a given fraction of rows of the data set?

accepted.question_text: Given a pattern class P and two similar data sets d and d', find a representation that concisely describes which patterns from P hold in d' when the user already knows which patterns from P hold in d. Equivalently, explain the differences between d and d' from the perspective of the pattern class P.

evidence.quote: Problem 2 Given a class P of patterns and two data sets d and d’, find a good way of representing the patterns of P that are true in d’, assuming the user knows the patterns that are true in d. That is, explain the differences between d and d’ (from the point of view of the pattern class P).

accepted.question_text: For sequences of events, identify a concept class together with an algorithm that can learn simple global descriptions of those sequences, rather than only partial local sequential patterns.

evidence.quote: Problem 3 Find a good concept class and algorithm for learning simple global descriptions of sequences of events.

accepted.question_text: For mixture modeling methods used in data mining, determine what can be proved about the computational complexity of the mixture-modeling problem.

evidence.quote: Problem 4 Can anything be said about computational complexity of the mixture modeling problem?

accepted.question_text: Frequent sets can be used to induce probability distributions by the maximum-entropy method. Are there other methods for inducing distributions from frequent sets, and if so, what alternative principles or algorithms can do this?

evidence.quote: Problem 5 Maximum entropy is a way of inducing distributions from frequent sets. Are there other approaches for the same task?

accepted.question_text: Let s be a long string, let σ be a threshold, and for each string w let h(w) denote the number of occurrences of w as a substring of s. If one knows h(w) for every substring w whose count is at least σ, what information about the original string s is determined or recoverable from that thresholded substring-count data?

evidence.quote: Problem 6 Given a long string s and a threshold σ. For a string w, denote by h(w) the number of times w occurs as a substring in s. Suppose we know h(w) for all w such that h(w) ≥ σ. What do we know about the string s?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a ground set and let L be a collection of subsets of R such that every X in L has size s. The upper shadow ∂L is the collection of all (s+1)-element sets whose every s-element subset lies in L. What is the computational complexity of computing this upper shadow from L?

evidence.quote: Problem 7 (Not very important.) Given a collection L of subsets of R such that for all X ∈ L we have |X| = s. The upper shadow [10] ∂L of L is the collection of sets of size s + 1 whose all subsets are in L. What is the complexity of computing the upper shadow?

accepted.question_text: Let α be an arbitrary Boolean query, and suppose Proposition 8 expresses the number g(α, d) of rows in a data set d satisfying α as a linear combination g(α, d) = Σ_i u_i f(X_i, d), where each X_i is a set of attributes and f(X_i, d) is the frequency of rows satisfying all attributes in X_i. How large must the integer coefficients u_i be in such representations?

evidence.quote: Proposition 8 For any boolean query α there exists sets Xi and coefficients ui such that for any dataset d we have g(α, d) = Σi uif(Xi, d) ... Problem 9 (Not very important.) How large do the coefficients ui have to be in the expression of Proposition 8?

accepted.question_text: Let α be a Boolean formula and let g(α, d) be the exact value given by the inclusion-exclusion expansion from Proposition 8 on a data set d. If D is a family of frequent sets and g_D(α, d) is the truncated sum obtained by keeping only terms coming from sets in D, how large can the approximation error e(α, D) = |g(α) − g_D(α)| be as a function of structural properties of D and of α?

evidence.quote: Problem 10 Given a Boolean formula α, consider the inclusion-exclusion description of g(α, d) given in Proposition 8. Let gD(, α, d) be the sum when only frequent sets from D are considered. How large can the the approximation error e(α, D) = |g(α) − gD(α)| be as a function of structural properties of D and α.

accepted.question_text: Let D be a downward-closed collection of subsets of a set R. Define the positive border Bd⁺(D) to be the maximal elements of D and the negative border Bd⁻(D) to be the minimal elements of P(R) \ D. For the conjunction α = ∧_{A∈X} A, is it always true that the approximation error from truncated inclusion-exclusion satisfies e(α, D) ≤ Σ_{Y∈Bd⁺(D)} f(Y) + Σ_{Y∈Bd⁻(D)} f(Y)?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 11 For α = ∧A∈X A we have e(α, D) ≤ ΣY ∈Bd+(D) f(Y ) + ΣY ∈Bd−(D) f(Y ).

accepted.question_text: If D is a downward-closed collection of subsets, is it always true that the alternating sum over its nonempty members is bounded by the total number of positive- and negative-border elements, namely Σ_{∅≠Y∈D} (−1)^{|Y|+1} ≤ |Bd⁺(D)| + |Bd⁻(D)|?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 12 For downwards closed collection D we have Σ∅≠Y ∈D (−1)|Y |+1 ≤ |Bd+(D)| + |Bd−(D)|

accepted.question_text: Given a hypergraph, a transversal is a minimal set of vertices that intersects every edge. Is there an algorithm that enumerates all transversals in time polynomial in the combined size of the input hypergraph and the output list of transversals?

evidence.quote: Problem 13 Find a polynomial time algorithm (in the size of the input and output) for enumerating all transversals.

accepted.question_text: Latent semantic indexing (LSI) is used for high-dimensional sparse discrete data such as document collections. Why does LSI work for discrete data, and what theoretical explanation accounts for its empirical effectiveness in that setting?

evidence.quote: Problem 14 Why does LSI (latent semantic indexing) [17] work for discrete data?

accepted.question_text: Randomized rounding appears to work very well for computing low-rank approximations. What are the precise limits and valid operating regimes of this approach for such approximation problems?

evidence.quote: Problem 15 Randomized rounding [1] seems to work very well for computing low-rank approximations. What are the boundaries of this approach?

accepted.question_text: Let R be a relation schema, let Q be a class of Boolean queries on data sets over R, and let k be an integer. Find k Boolean queries α₁, ..., α_k such that, for every data set d over R, the answers to α₁, ..., α_k on d suffice to answer every query β in Q on the same data set.

evidence.quote: Problem 16 Given a relation schema R and a class of boolean queries Q for datasets over R and an integer k. Find k queries α1,...,αk such that for all datasets d over R we can answer any query β ∈ Q on d using the answers of αi on d.

accepted.question_text: Let S = {B₁, ..., B_p} be attributes where each attribute B_i takes values in a finite domain D_i. Find a principled way to define similarity between values inside each finite domain D_i.

evidence.quote: Problem 17 Given a set of attributes S = {B1,...,Bp}, where each Bi can obtain values from a finite domain Di, find a good way of defining the similarity of values in each Di.

accepted.question_text: What constitutes a good theoretical framework for data mining?

evidence.quote: Problem 18 What is a good theoretical framework for data mining?

accepted.question_text: Develop and characterize the limits of data-mining methods that are provably privacy-preserving; in particular, determine where the boundaries of provably privacy-preserving data mining lie.

evidence.quote: Problem 19 Explore the boundaries of provably privacy-preserving data mining.

trace.notes: Resolved the zbMATH record through the DOI 10.1007/3-540-45465-9_6 to a readable Springer PDF and mapped the open-problem region to pages 6-9, with a preview open-question sentence on page 5.
Extracted the explicit numbered Problem 1-19 items from pages 7-9 and the two explicit conjectures on page 8 as open research questions.
Expanded notation and ambient setting directly into question_text where needed so each accepted item is self-contained without referring back to the paper.
The page-5 sentence about |g(α) − gD(α)| appears to preview the fuller Problem 10 statement, but the wording is not identical, so it was moved to needs_review rather than merged automatically.
